newsitem.title: USA: Turkey rating set for cut or confirmation - Moody's.
newsitem.headline: Turkey rating set for cut or confirmation - Moody's.

text.p: Turkey's Ba3 foreign currency rating is set for either a rating downgrade or confirmation by Moody's Investors Service Inc but no announcement has been made yet, said a senior analyst with the sovereign risk group at Moody's in New York.

"There will be a rating action in the sense of either a confirmation or downgrade sometime in the near future. There is not much more that I can say than that" but no announcement has been reached yet, the analyst told Reuters in a telephone interview.

The Moody's analyst, who did not want to be named, said having placed the rating under review, it usually takes an average of about two months to "complete our analysis, make a decision and follow that up with an announcement either of a confirmation at the present rating of Ba3 or a downgrade."
He said concerns about Turkey's fiscal policy and economic policy in general prompted Moody's to place the country's foreign currency rating under review on January 9.

The analyst said Moody's has not yet rated Turkey's local currency. "It's our intention during the course of the year to announce local currency ratings for all of our sovereigns but very few have been announced as yet."
